clue.text: Rebellions in film about disruption Germany stops

indicators.note: about means going round, so the film word wraps the rest
something that stops a gap plugs it, so the country's letter sits inside the disruption word

blocks.note: a film is a thin coat or layer
an upset is a disruption
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A film reviewer notes that a movie about a German upheaval features uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: The German letter is plugged into the disruption first, and the film word then wraps the result; the French phrase means a strike against the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Coups d'etat are sudden seizures of government power, a form of rebellion against the ruling regime.

clue.text: Persuade military chief over peace, yielding power …

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the chief comes first
yielding means giving up, so the letter for power is surrendered

blocks.note: CO is a commanding officer
pax is Latin for peace
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone talks a general into accepting peace at the cost of giving up power.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, where 'yielding power' is applied a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade gently, wheedling someone into doing something.

clue.text: … in removal of rivals? Persuade insistently

indicators.note: the ellipsis carries over the previous clue's yielding power, which applies again in this case

blocks.note: a purge is the removal of political rivals

explanation.surface: Continuing the military theme: a dictator, after purging rivals, presses others hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis borrows 'yielding power' from 1 Down, so the letter P (power) is given up here too.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge is to press or encourage someone strongly to do something.

clue.text: Representation of life and arts around Amsterdam? Rembrandt's speciality

indicators.note: a representation renders its subject in a new form, so these letters are rearranged
around means the rearranged letters surround the city clue

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Amsterdam is a port, defined by example as the question mark admits

explanation.surface: An art-historical note on the Dutch master's depictions of life and his city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rembrandt painted dozens of pictures of himself, so the definition is a fact about him rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt is famous for the many paintings he made of his own face across his career.

clue.text: Naked, uncovered – regret turning up shouting this?

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go
in a down clue turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the word naked with its outer letters removed
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Archimedes, leaping from his bath, ran naked through the streets shouting, perhaps regretting it.
explanation.walkthrough: AKE and RUE are read upwards to give EUREKA. The whole clue evokes Archimedes, who ran naked from his bath crying the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eureka is the cry of discovery Archimedes is said to have shouted while running unclothed.

clue.text: Music for instrument (not piano) is test showing skill

indicators.note: not says the letter standing for piano, quiet in music, is left out

blocks.note: a part is the music written for one instrument
p is the musical marking for soft
taken as written
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: An orchestral player's score, minus the piano part, is an exam that reveals ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or craftsmanship, especially in performance.

clue.text: Scratching head, dispose of irritation

indicators.note: scratching here means striking out, so the first letter is crossed off

blocks.note: to ditch is to get rid of

explanation.surface: Scratching your scalp gets rid of an annoying tickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' reads as relieving an itchy scalp; it is the instruction to cut the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a skin irritation that makes you want to scratch.

clue.text: Satanic mill mostly abandoned as an indicator of good luck

definitions.text: as an indicator of good luck
definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: taken as written
mill without its last letter

explanation.surface: Blake's dark Satanic mills, deserted, are oddly taken as a lucky omen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Blake's 'dark Satanic mills' from the hymn Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a charm believed to bring good fortune, so talismanic means serving as such a charm.

clue.text: Arrest after journo snaps leaders of Ealing Young Conservatives in hired vehicle

indicators.note: after places the arrest word behind the journalist word
leaders are those at the front, so only initial letters are taken
to snap up is to catch hold, so the arrest word grabs the initials inside it

blocks.note: a hack is a journalist, usually a jobbing one
to nab is to arrest
initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A photographer snaps local Tory youth in a taxi, followed by an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: HACK then NAB holding EYC gives HACKNEY CAB. Ealing and Hackney are both London boroughs, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney cab is the formal name for a London taxi, a vehicle hired for a journey.

clue.text: A quirk, ignoring South Island jaggedness

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letters for South and Island are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a singularity is a peculiarity or quirk
S for South and I for Island

explanation.surface: A geographical oddity: a quirk of the map that leaves out New Zealand's South Island.
explanation.walkthrough: South Island reads as the New Zealand place name, but it is just two abbreviations to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Angularity is the quality of having sharp corners or angles, hence jaggedness of outline.

clue.text: Several parties back horse, putting in pounds

indicators.note: back means the horse word is read backwards
putting in means inserting the pounds letter into the other word

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from libra

explanation.surface: A political coalition backs a racehorse with a sizeable cash bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like betting on the horse; it means reversing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of parties or nations acting together.

clue.text: One of top four if included in shortened version of important register

indicators.note: a shortened version has a letter cut out, here one of the doubled letters at the join
included in means placed inside the longer word

blocks.note: seminal means highly influential or important
a register is a list
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cup contender's place in the last four is recorded in an abridged official roll.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words run together share a doubled letter at the join; shortening drops one of them before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinalist is a competitor among the last four, contesting the semifinals.

clue.text: Delegate incites legislators to ignore a European in singular issue?

indicators.note: to ignore is to leave out, so the European letter goes
in places everything before it inside the offspring word

blocks.note: to poke is to prod or goad
peers sit in the House of Lords and make laws
E is the abbreviation for European
issue means offspring, and one son is a single child

explanation.surface: A delegate stirs up lawmakers to snub a European over one particular question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a topic for debate but means offspring; legislators here are members of the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesperson speaks on behalf of others, acting as their delegate or representative.

clue.text: Focus of casting decisions? Mostly dubious, in brief

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in places the shortened word inside the other

blocks.note: fishy means suspicious or dubious
a flying visit is a brief one

explanation.surface: Choosing actors for roles is mostly questionable, to put it briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting decisions' suggests a director picking actors; an angler casting a line chooses which fly to use.
explanation.definitionFit: In fly-fishing the angler casts an artificial fly, so choosing the cast is central to the sport.

clue.text: Say one's thoughts: talk rudely about husband in upset couple

indicators.note: rudely means roughly or crudely, so the letters are knocked about
about means the mixed-up letters go round the next part
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written
a duo is a couple

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a husband during a couple's row lays bare what one thinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the four letters of the talk word are mixed; they keep the husband and the little word inside, and the turned couple follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To think aloud is to voice one's thoughts as they occur, speaking them out.

clue.text: Traditional stories about a hospital in Pakistani city

indicators.note: about means the stories word wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: lore is a body of traditional stories
taken as written
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Folk tales told about a hospital in a South Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province and Pakistan's second largest city.

clue.text: Standard right-winger, ignoring leader, receiving money from Arab country

indicators.note: ignoring the leader means the first letter is not used
receiving means taking in, so the currency goes inside

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative
the dinar is the currency of several Arab states such as Iraq and Jordan

explanation.surface: A typical conservative, sidelined by the party leader, takes Gulf money.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY loses its T and the remaining ORY takes in DINAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard and ordinary both describe something usual, normal or without special features.

clue.text: Hopeful and reasonable about one in care of Rev?

indicators.note: about means the reasonable word goes round everything that follows
something in the care of another is held by it, so the one sits inside

blocks.note: sane means sensible or reasonable
to gun an engine is to rev it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cheerful, sensible vicar looks after a parishioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like a clergyman; it is the verb, as in gunning or revving an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine means optimistic and confident, especially in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Entertainment not imagined to suppress energy associated with death

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down within, so the energy letter is shut inside

blocks.note: fun is entertainment
E is the physics symbol for energy
real means not imaginary

explanation.surface: Genuine amusement quashes high spirits at a sombre occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Funereal means suited to a funeral, gloomy and solemn, so connected with death.

clue.text: A car reversed on beginning to move the smallest distances?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
in an across clue on means placed after
reversed means the article and the car are read backwards

blocks.note: the first letter of move
taken as written
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A small car backs up just as it starts to move, covering very short distances.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that minima need not be distances; the car theme suggests it.
explanation.definitionFit: Minima is the plural of minimum, the least possible amounts, here applied to distance.

clue.text: Contest interrupted by Republican scare

indicators.note: interrupted by means something breaks in, so a letter is inserted

blocks.note: a fight is a contest
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An election race disrupted by a Republican candidate causes alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden scare or shock of fear.

clue.text: Laugh about possessing male toiletry

indicators.note: about means the laugh word wraps round the possessing word

blocks.note: a scream is something hilarious, a laugh
having means possessing

explanation.surface: A man laughs at owning a particular bathroom product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It was a scream' means it was a laugh, which is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaving cream is lathered on before shaving, a toiletry traditionally used by men.

clue.text: One drink excluded from initial examination

indicators.note: excluded from means taken out of, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: original means first or initial
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A student is barred from a first exam for having one drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial examination' looks like the definition; initial is the wordplay word and examination alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in language exams or medical vivas.

clue.text: Little bird not previously seen soaring around river

indicators.note: in a down clue soaring means rising, so the letters read upwards
around means the turned word encloses the river letter

blocks.note: something new has not been seen before
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a small, never-before-seen bird flying high over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaring' fits the bird in the picture; it is the upward-reading signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wren is one of Britain's smallest birds, a tiny brown songbird.

clue.text: Charged material covering source of rare item on course

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter
covering means wrapping round, so the charged word encloses the letter

blocks.note: an ion is an electrically charged particle
the first letter of rare

explanation.surface: A lab note: charged stuff wrapped round a rare object used on a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a golf course; an iron is one of the clubs a golfer carries.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a type of golf club, one of the items a player uses on the course.

clue.text: Judge restricting northern newspaper, one offering a backward look

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the judge word holds the northern letter

blocks.note: a judge wears a wig, so wig stands for a judge
N is the abbreviation for northern
the Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A judge gags a regional newspaper that publishes retrospectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A backward look' suggests a nostalgic column, but it means a car's side mirror showing what is behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing mirror is mounted on a car's side to let the driver see traffic behind.

clue.text: English critical comment set back French author

indicators.note: set back means placed in the opposite direction, read right to left

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a dig is a cutting remark

explanation.surface: An English reviewer's barbed remark delayed a writer from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate, author of The Immoralist.

clue.text: Physical training in moorland leads to losing one new Olympic event

indicators.note: in places the training letters inside the moorland word
leads are the front letters, so the first letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: a heath is open moorland
PT is physical training
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Running drills on the moor point to an athlete dropping out of a recently introduced Games event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads to' looks like causation; it means the leading letters of the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The heptathlon is a seven-event athletics contest for women at the Olympic Games.
